course_subtitle: Develop your own games like a pro! 🎮✨

stations.title: Station 1: Welcome to the Magical World of Godot! 🏰
stations.desc: A delightful introduction to game engines and the fun world of Godot with Toby the Teddy Bear!
stations.story:
🧸 Hello, creative game developer!

I am your friend Toby the Teddy Bear, and I will accompany you on your journey to build your very first game! 🌟

Today we will discover the magic of the Godot Engine! A game engine is like a magical toy box containing everything we need to build games (movement tools, sounds, and colorful art!).

💡 Golden Knowledge from our official curriculum:
  • 🏗️ Node: Like a small colorful Lego block, it is the building block of every part of your game!
  • 🏰 Scene: Like a big playroom where we gather all the Lego blocks (Nodes) to build a complete world!
  • 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Father-Child Structure: The Child node inherits properties from its Parent node, just like a child following their loving parent's steps!
🧸 Toby's Challenge: Let's welcome the magical world of Godot by writing a sweet welcome message inside the start function _ready()!
stations.simple: A game engine is the magical toy box of games, and nodes are the colorful Lego blocks we use to build our dreams!
stations.hint: Write the magical welcome message: print("Welcome to the fun world of Godot!")
stations.challenge: Add code to print Toby's sweet welcome: `Welcome to the fun world of Godot!` inside the start function.

pills.label: Toby's Welcome
pills.code: print("Welcome to the fun world of Godot!")

validation_rules.required_output_text: Welcome to the fun world of Godot!

homework.title: 🏠 Magic Home Challenge: Creator's First Message
homework.desc: Write code that prints your hero name with a sweet Godot welcome to finalize your first steps!

stations.title: Station 2: Secret Codes and Smart Variables! 📝
stations.desc: Learn the magic language of GDScript, variable boxes, and wake-up functions with Dino the Dinosaur!
stations.story:
🦖 Welcome, coding artist!

I am your friend Dino the little Dinosaur, and today we will learn how to whisper secret words that Godot understands instantly! 🌟

We use a lovely and simple coding language called GDScript, which is very similar to Python. It lets us control our heroes and make them move and jump!

💡 Magic Info Capsule:
  • 📦 Variable: Like a smart box where we store the hero's energy or score. We use the magic word var to create it!
  • 🔢 Primitive Data Types:
    • int: Sweet whole numbers like the hero's hearts 5!
    • float: Precise decimal numbers like gravity speed 9.8!
    • bool: Magical choices (true or false) like 'is the hero flying?'
  • ⏳ Special Functions: _ready() runs once at the beginning to wake up our heroes, and _process(delta) runs at lightning speed to update game actions constantly!
🦖 Dino's Challenge: Let's create Dino's sweet energy box with a value of 100 and print it for everyone to see!
stations.simple: A variable is a magical box to store our heroes' energy, and GDScript is the language we use to tell Godot to move!
stations.hint: Define the energy variable: var energy = 100 and then print it: print(energy)
stations.challenge: Define a variable named `energy` with a value of `100` and print it inside the ready function.

homework.title: 🏠 Magic Home Challenge: Hero Heart Box
homework.desc: Define a variable for the hero's hearts holding a value of 3 and print it at home to assist Dino!
homework.code:
extends Node

func _ready():
    var hearts = 3
    print("Hero hearts count: ", hearts)

stations.title: Station 3: The Little Artist and Animated Sprites! 🎨
stations.desc: Design gorgeous 2D game worlds, Sprite nodes, and frame animation sheets with Kitty the active Kitten!
stations.story:
🐱 Welcome, creative artist!

I am your friend Kitty the active Kitten, and today we will decorate our game with the most beautiful visual drawings and vibrant colors! ✨

To make our game come alive, let's learn about art styles and animated frames!

💡 Art & Animation Secrets from our PDFs:
  • 🎨 Art Styles: Cartoonish style full of bright colors, Pixel Art with classic retro vibes, and smooth Hand-Drawn drawings!
  • 🖼️ Sprite Node: The node responsible for displaying any static (fixed) image in our lovely game.
  • 🏃‍♀️ AnimatedSprite Node: Our magical node that displays the hero's actions frame-by-frame (Frame Animation) to make them look like they are running and jumping!
  • 📜 Sprite Sheet: One large image containing all the hero's moves combined to save computer memory!
🐱 Kitty's Challenge: Kitty is running at a speed of 150! Let's print it to cheer her up!
stations.simple: AnimatedSprite combines consecutive images to make characters run, and colorful art makes players happy!
stations.hint: Write the print statement for Kitty's speed: print("Kitty's active speed is: 150")
stations.challenge: Print the following text exactly: `Kitty's active speed is: 150`

homework.title: 🏠 Magic Home Challenge: Animation Frames
homework.desc: Write code that prints the number of running frames of our hero (e.g. 8 frames) to help Kitty organize her sprite sheet!
homework.code:
extends Node

func _ready():
    var run_frames = 8
    print("Hero running frames: ", run_frames)

stations.title: Station 4: Speedy Bunny and Smart Operators! 🐰
stations.desc: Program speedy movement, mathematical operations, logic rules, and sizing with the set_scale function!
stations.story:
🐰 Welcome, my fast and smart friend!

I am your friend Speedy Bunny, and today we will learn the magic language of math that moves our games and makes heroes jump and spin! 🌟

To design smart movement, we will use arithmetic and comparisons!

💡 Magic Math Box:
  • ➕ Arithmetic Operators: Addition +, Subtraction -, Multiplication *, and Division / to decide speeds and distances!
  • ⚖️ Comparison Operators: Check if speed equals 50 (==), does not equal (!=), is greater than (>), or less than (<).
  • 🛡️ Logical Operators: Combine conditions like (and, or, not) to set game rules precisely!
  • 📐 set_scale function: We use set_scale(Vector2(x, y)) to resize our lovely characters!
🐰 Bunny's Challenge: Bunny runs at a basic speed of 50, we want to double it by multiplying it by 2 and print his new speed 100!
stations.simple: Arithmetic operations and logical conditions are the smart brain that decides when Bunny jumps and when he resizes!
stations.hint: Multiply the basic speed by 2 and print the result: print("Speedy Bunny's new speed is: ", base_speed * 2)
stations.challenge: Define a variable `base_speed = 50` and multiply it by 2, then print: `Speedy Bunny's new speed is: 100`
stations.starter_code:
extends Node

func _ready():
    var base_speed = 50
    # Double the speed and print the result here!

pills.label: Double Speed & Print
pills.code:
var double_speed = base_speed * 2
    print("Speedy Bunny's new speed is: ", double_speed)

homework.title: 🏠 Magic Home Challenge: Is Bunny a Giant?
homework.desc: Compare the size of the paddle or Bunny, and print a boolean status using comparisons in code!
homework.code:
extends Node

func _ready():
    var is_giant = true
    print("Is Speedy Bunny a giant? ", is_giant)

stations.title: Station 5: Journey of a Game from Idea to Light! 💡🌱
stations.desc: How do professional game engineers plan? Learn the SDLC phases and prototype your very first concept with Philo!
stations.story:
🐘 Welcome, genius game engineer!

I am your friend Philo the smart Elephant! Today we will learn how game developers plan their incredible games! 🌟

Making a game is not just coding, it is an organized journey called the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)!

💡 The 6 Magic Stages of SDLC:
  • 💡 1. Idea Generation: Brainstorming ideas for our exciting game story!
  • 🛠️ 2. Prototyping: Building a quick, simple version to make sure the gameplay is fun!
  • 🎨 3. Design: Designing art, characters, and sounds!
  • 💻 4. Development: Writing the real GDScript code in Godot!
  • 🧪 5. Testing: Playing the game to find and fix bugs!
  • 🚀 6. Release: Sharing our game with friends and the world!
🐘 Philo's Challenge: Print the first and most fundamental stage of game development!
stations.simple: SDLC is the magical map that transforms a simple idea into a real, playable game!
stations.hint: Write the print statement: print("The first step is idea generation!")
stations.challenge: Print the following text exactly: `The first step is idea generation!`

pills.label: Print First Stage
pills.code: print("The first step is idea generation!")

validation_rules.required_output_text: The first step is idea generation!

homework.title: 🏠 Magic Home Challenge: Testing Games
homework.desc: Write code printing the importance of testing games to eliminate bugs and avoid game crashes!

stations.title: Station 6: Magical Buttons and Colorful Panels! 🖥️
stations.desc: Discover the attractive world of UI nodes, Labels, Buttons, LineEdits, and layout Containers with Susu!
stations.story:
🐦 Welcome, visual panel designer!

I am your friend Susu the singing Bird! Today we will learn to build UI panels to display scores, health, and buttons! 🌟

The User Interface (UI) is how players interact with our game!

💡 UI Nodes & Containers:
  • 📝 Label Node: Displays text on the screen like score or player name!
  • 🔘 Button Node: An interactive button players click to start or purchase items!
  • 📥 LineEdit: A box where players can type their name!
  • 📦 Containers: VBoxContainer organizes buttons vertically, and HBoxContainer organizes them horizontally!
🐦 Susu's Challenge: Let's print the score panel text Score: 50 to display it!
stations.simple: Label nodes display sweet text like scores, and Buttons open the gates of interactive gameplay!
stations.challenge: Print the following text exactly to show the score: `Score: 50`

homework.title: 🏠 Magic Home Challenge: Start Button Trigger
homework.desc: Write code simulating the message printed when the start button is clicked (e.g. game launched)!

stations.title: Station 7: Signal Language and Interactive Buttons! 📡
stations.desc: Program button triggers, scene switching, quitting functions, and connect Godot signals with Maymoon!
stations.story:
🐒 Welcome, smart interactive programmer!

I am your friend Maymoon the playful Monkey! Today we will make our games alive by responding to player clicks! 🌟

When a player clicks buttons, we use a genius system in Godot called Signals to tell the game what to do immediately!

💡 Signals & Scene Control:
  • 📡 Signals: A way for nodes to send events (like pressed() from a Button) to trigger code!
  • 🔄 Scene Switching: Switch from main menu to game scene using: get_tree().change_scene("res://Scenes/Game.tscn")!
  • 🚪 Quitting: Exit the game peacefully using get_tree().quit()!
🐒 Maymoon's Challenge: Let's simulate switching to the game scene by printing the confirmation message!
stations.simple: Signals are magical telephone lines that call code immediately when a player clicks a button to switch scenes!
stations.hint: Print the scene switch message: print("Scene changed to Game.tscn")
stations.challenge: Print the following text exactly to simulate switching scenes: `Scene changed to Game.tscn`

homework.title: 🏠 Magic Home Challenge: Quit Game Trigger
homework.desc: Write code printing a simulation of quitting the game when players click Exit, using get_tree().quit()!

stations.title: Station 8: Joyful Sounds and Dreamy Music! 🎵
stations.desc: Add exciting sound effects, dreamy background music, and trigger AudioStreamPlayer2D with Shahdour!
stations.story:
🐶 Welcome, creative sound engineer!

I am your friend Shahdour the sweet Puppy! Today we will add sound effects and music to make our game joyful! 🌟

Sound in games increases fun and makes players feel the actions!

💡 Golden Sound Box:
  • 💥 Sound Effects (SFX): Short sounds like jumping, bouncing, or scoring!
  • 🎶 Background Music (BGM): Continuous music playing in the background to set the game mood!
  • 📢 AudioStreamPlayer2D Node: The node responsible for playing sound files in Godot.
  • 🎛️ Properties: Stream holds the sound file, Volume controls loudness, and Pitch controls speed/tone!
  • 🎮 Functions: We use play() to start the sound and stop() to stop it!
🐶 Shahdour's Challenge: Let's simulate playing the jumping sound by printing the play message!
stations.simple: AudioStreamPlayer2D plays sweet sounds using play() and stop() to make our games alive and interactive!
stations.hint: Print the sound playing message: print("Playing sweet sound!")
stations.challenge: Print the following text exactly: `Playing sweet sound!`

homework.title: 🏠 Magic Home Challenge: Stop Music
homework.desc: Write code simulating the stopping of background music by calling stop() on our audio players!

stations.title: Station 9: Magic Camera and Moving Backgrounds! 📸🌌
stations.desc: Follow players smoothly, design deep parallax scrolling backgrounds, and load assets with Battoota!
stations.story:
🦆 Welcome, visual world explorer!

I am your friend Battoota the swimming Duck! Today we will make our game world vast and learn the secrets of cameras! 🌟

The camera is the player's eye inside our game, allowing them to explore big worlds!

💡 Camera & Background Secrets:
  • 📸 Camera2D Node: A camera node that follows our player when current is set to true!
  • ✨ Smoothing: A setting that makes the camera follow the player smoothly without stuttering!
  • 🌌 Parallax Background: A layered background where far layers move slower than near layers to create depth!
  • 📜 preload: A magic method like preload("res://RainDrop.tscn") that loads assets into memory before playing to avoid lag!
🦆 Battoota's Challenge: Let's simulate preloading a raindrop asset by printing the success message!
stations.simple: Cameras follow the player smoothly, and Parallax backgrounds create amazing depth in our game worlds!
stations.hint: Print the preloading success message: print("Raindrop loaded successfully!")
stations.challenge: Print the following text exactly to confirm the preload: `Raindrop loaded successfully!`

homework.title: 🏠 Magic Home Challenge: Camera Tracking Active
homework.desc: Write code that checks and prints the camera tracking status, verifying current is active at home!
homework.code:
extends Node

func _ready():
    var camera_active = true
    print("Is Camera2D active tracking? ", camera_active)

stations.title: Station 10: Polishing Games and Launching to the Universe! 🚀✨
stations.desc: Master game polishing, responsiveness, exporting to HTML5, and sharing free games on itch.io with Sanjoob!
stations.story:
🐿️ Welcome, future game publisher!

I am your friend Sanjoob the explorer Squirrel! Today we will polish our game, fix all bugs, and make it ready to play on the web! 🌟

Polishing is the final creative touch that makes players happy and removes errors!

💡 Polishing & Publishing Secrets:
  • ✨ Polishing Factors:
    • ❤️ Fun Factor: Is the game highly entertaining and makes players want to play again?
    • 🕹️ Responsiveness: Immediate reaction to inputs and buttons!
    • 🌱 Liveliness: Making the world active with visual effects and movements!
  • 🛠️ Exporting: Choose Project -> Export and select HTML5 to run the game in web browsers!
  • 🌐 itch.io: The best free website to upload, publish, and share our games with friends!
🐿️ Sanjoob's Challenge: Let's print that our game is fully polished and ready for publishing!
stations.simple: Polishing removes bugs and makes games fun, and HTML5 export allows everyone to play instantly in a web browser!
stations.hint: Print the readiness message: print("Game is polished and ready!")
stations.challenge: Print the following text exactly: `Game is polished and ready!`

homework.title: 🏠 Magic Home Challenge: Export Steps
homework.desc: Write code printing the three golden steps of exporting projects in Godot to web platforms!

stations.title: Station 11: Birth of the Legendary Pong Game - Part 1! 🏓
stations.desc: Build the lovely Pong field, physics boundaries, moving player paddles, and keyboard input maps with Toby!
stations.story:
🧸 Welcome, game builder champion!

I am your friend Toby the Teddy Bear! Today we start building a classic masterpiece: The Pong Game! 🌟

Pong is a fun duel between two players using paddles to hit a ball!

💡 Pong Foundations in Godot:
  • 🧱 StaticBody2D (Walls): Strong physical walls that do not move, keeping the ball inside the screen!
  • 🏓 KinematicBody2D (Paddles & Ball): Physical bodies we control with code so they respond to inputs!
  • ⌨️ Inputs: Left paddle moves with W / S keys, and right paddle moves with Up / Down Arrows!
🧸 Toby's Challenge: Let's write the code to print that the paddle is moving upward!
stations.simple: StaticBody2D boundaries protect the ball, and KinematicBody2D paddles move with keyboard keys to block the ball!
stations.hint: Print the paddle moving upward: print("Moving paddle up")
stations.challenge: Print the following text exactly: `Moving paddle up`

homework.title: 🏠 Magic Home Challenge: Ball Initial Speed
homework.desc: Define the ball's initial speed variable at home and print it to prepare for the ball launching!
homework.code:
extends Node

func _ready():
    var ball_speed = 300
    print("Initial ball speed set to: ", ball_speed)

stations.title: Station 12: Return of Pong and the Ultimate Climax - Part 2! 🏆💥
stations.desc: Program collision triggers, bounce physics, update scoreboard labels, and sketch trailer concepts with Toby!
stations.story:
🏆 You are a game developing champion!

I am your friend Toby the Teddy Bear! Today we finish our Pong game with scores, ball bounces, and trailers! 🌟

To complete the excitement, we will code collision reflections and track points!

💡 Pong Physics & Climax:
  • 💥 Area2D (Collisions): A node that detects when the ball enters the goal or hits paddles!
  • 🔄 Ball Bounce Physics: We reflect the ball's direction by multiplying its speed by negative one (speed.x = -speed.x)!
  • 📊 Updating Score: We update the Label node immediately when the ball scores a point!
  • 🎬 Game Trailer: A short, exciting video clip showcasing our game to invite players on itch.io!
🧸 Toby's Final Challenge: Let's code the bounce of the ball off the paddle and print the message!
stations.simple: Area2D detects collisions, bounce math reflects the ball direction, and labels display scores!
stations.hint: Print the bounce message: print("Ball bounced off the paddle!")
stations.challenge: Print the following text exactly: `Ball bounced off the paddle!`

homework.title: 🏠 Magic Home Challenge: Game Slogan Idea
homework.desc: Create a short and engaging marketing slogan for your Pong game and print it with joy!
